messages:
anya.k: Quick q — I'm updating the offline bundle RFC. Thinking about aligning chunk_size to MTU to avoid IP-level fragmentation when transferring seed bundles across customer networks. Tradeoffs: larger chunks = fewer hashes / less manifest bloat, but more memory for verifier and worse retransmit cost on flaky links. Thoughts?

mike_r: Aligning to MTU makes sense for point-to-point transfers, but many customer appliances will tunnel (GRE/VPN) so MTU varies. We need a safe default (e.g., 64KiB) and a per-transport clamp.

sanjay: Agree on clamp. Also important: choose streaming verification so verifier doesn't need to hold full chunk set in RAM. We can do incremental BLAKE3 while reassembling.

lisa: Short note on reassembly_window — if a chunk is split across packets and reordering happens, we need a resequencing buffer. Too large = memory blowup on low-memory devices. Too small = false failures on high-latency networks.

anya.k: Good points. Proposed defaults in the RFC draft:
```
chunk_size_bytes: 65536
max_in_flight_chunks: 6
reassembly_window_ms: 2500
verification_mode: streaming_hash
hash_algorithm: blake3
```
Would that be conservative enough?

mike_r: Seems fine. max_in_flight_chunks is the key backpressure knob. On slow links reduce to 2-3. Also add a rate_hint header so sender reduces concurrency: `X-Chunk-Window: 3`.

sanjay: +1 on X-Chunk-Window. Implementation note: sender should honor a `429`-like transport response with `Retry-After-ms` for soft backpressure. For retries use exponential backoff with jitter: base 250ms, factor 2, max 10s, max_retries 7.

lisa: For verifier memory: prefer streaming verify + fixed-size chunk buffer. If device memory < 256MB switch to a 'lowmem' mode: chunk_size=32KiB, max_in_flight=2. Add autodetect in agent startup.

anya.k: What about manifest design? Current manifest lists chunk digests + length + sequence. Do we need additional per-chunk metadata (orig_mtu_hint, compressed_len)?

sanjay: Add compression flag + compressed_len; origin MTU_hint is noisy. Better: include transport profile name (e.g., tcp, http, rsync) at manifest header level.

mike_r: Also include `chunk_id` deterministic (content-addressed) and `seq_num` for ordering. That lets verifier stream-verify while reordering by seq_num.

lisa: Security: verify each chunk signature (or sign the manifest and verify chunk digests only). Per-chunk sigs cost CPU and size. I think manifest-signed + blake3 digests is sufficient if transport integrity is not trusted.

anya.k: Actionable items:
- Add lowmem mode heuristics and defaults to RFC draft (assigned @lisa)
- Add transport backpressure header + retry semantics to protocol section (assigned @mike_r)
- Add streaming-verifier reference pseudocode + blake3 note (assigned @sanjay)
- Update manifest schema to include compressed_len and transport_profile (I'll do a PR)

ops-bot: Created RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/722 (status: draft)

mike_r: I'll iterate on the backpressure section and add example client pseudocode:
```
// sender pseudocode
while (not done) {
  if (in_flight < X-Chunk-Window) send_next_chunk()
  else await 50ms or backpressure signal
}
```

anya.k: Thanks everyone. If no objections I'll fold these into the draft by EOD and tag security for a quick review. :thumbsup:

sanjay: No objections. One last perf note: measure blake3 streaming cost per 1MiB on t4g-like devices — might be our gating metric for lowmem thresholds.

lisa: Will run quick perf bench and post numbers in the PR.

anya.k: Closing thread here. Will ping when PR ready.
